_what_this_is: The BGL4 independent audit of the grades the earlier waves produced. Each row carries the verdict of an examiner whose instruction was to prove the grade wrong, plus what was attacked and what the command printed. Rows the audit could not settle are ABSENT from this file rather than present and unaudited, so they keep whatever their earlier wave recorded.
_why_this_matters: A grade nobody argued with is a claim, not a measurement. Measured over the earlier waves, better than one grade in five did not survive an independent check, which is the whole reason the release gate counts an unaudited grade as open work.

Root cause: The clamped 1.0 from minimum_detectable_effect is finite, so a design that can detect nothing was graded into the 'very low power' BAND instead of could-not-check, and the band sentence then printed a floor no difference of proportions can reach. The function also had no guard of its own on that sentence.. Before: power_warning(2,100) -> 'Very low statistical power (n=2). This test can only detect disparities larger than 100%. ...' while power_warning(0,100) and power_warning(1,100) -> 'Statistical power COULD NOT BE ASSESSED (n=0 / n=1) ...' for the same impossibility.. Root cause: The zero-variance guard was keyed on np.ptp and np.var of the target, and both are NaN when the target carries a NaN (nan == 0.0 is False, nan <= 0.0 is False), so the refusal was unreachable on a NaN-bearing target; the classification branch wrote accuracy_measured = True as a hardcoded literal and never revisited it, so on that path the flag could not be False at all. One guard placed ABOVE both branches now counts the rows neither branch can score, which is the same defect in both and is what makes the zero-variance guard reachable. Third defect, one layer up: full_analysis rebuilt baseline_metrics from three fields and dropped the flag, and NaN is not a state the rendering layer speaks.. Before: regression, y = np.arange(240) with y[3] = nan, y_pred = np.arange(240) -> accuracy nan with parameters['accuracy_measured'] True and NO warning. classification, y and y_pred both all NaN -> accuracy 0.0 with accuracy_measured True (nan == nan is False on every row, so 240 unscorable rows read as a model that got every row wrong). vfairness.operations.cicd.gate.ModelFair.judgement: Overturned on audit and then fixed. Root cause: improvement_amount returns None when a metric's better-direction is not declared, and both gate entry points substituted abs(baseline) - abs(value) for that None and decided `passed` from it. The substitution assumes smaller is better, so for any metric where larger is better the sign is backwards.. Before: value 0.2 baseline 0.3 published improvement 0.09999999999999998; value 0.3 baseline 0.2 published -0.09999999999999998; no warning in either case.. After: improvement is NaN (not None, which means no comparison was required), the unevaluated requirement is named in the decision, and the gate fails closed on it. Four sites in two entry points now share one helper.. Healthy control: A declared metric moving 0.3 to 0.2 is a measured improvement of exactly 0.1 and the gate approves; the same move backwards blocks with the real message; a gate with neither requirement configured keeps improvement None, which is the third state..
